questions.q: In full fine-tuning with Adam, what is typically the dominant source of GPU memory usage -- more than the model weights themselves?
options: The tokenizer vocabulary
Optimizer state -- Adam's two running moment estimates per parameter, usually kept in fp32
The dataset stored on disk
The chat template
questions.explain: Adam's optimizer state requires two additional per-parameter values (first and second moment), typically in fp32, which outweighs the memory used by the bf16 weights and gradients themselves.

questions.q: What does parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) do differently from full fine-tuning?
options: It trains on a larger dataset than full fine-tuning
It updates only a small subset or small number of newly added parameters, freezing the vast majority of the pretrained weights
It skips the forward pass entirely
It is only usable for pretraining, not fine-tuning
questions.explain: PEFT freezes almost all of the original pretrained weights and trains only a small number of parameters (such as LoRA's added low-rank matrices), rather than updating every parameter.

questions.q: Why does freezing most parameters produce such a large memory savings in PEFT, beyond just not updating those weights?
options: Frozen weights are deleted from GPU memory entirely
Gradients and optimizer state only need to be stored for the small trainable subset, not for the full parameter count -- and those are the dominant costs in full fine-tuning
Frozen weights no longer need to be loaded at all during inference
PEFT eliminates the need for a forward pass
questions.explain: Since gradients and optimizer state (the dominant memory costs) are only needed for trainable parameters, freezing most of the model dramatically shrinks those costs even though frozen weights are still loaded.

questions.q: What does `get_peft_model` do in the Hugging Face `peft` library?
options: It quantizes a model to 4-bit precision
It wraps a base model with a PEFT configuration (such as a LoraConfig), producing a model where only the added parameters are trainable
It converts a causal language model into a classification model
It merges two separately trained models into one
questions.explain: get_peft_model takes a base model and a PEFT configuration (e.g., LoraConfig) and returns a wrapped model where the specified adapter parameters are trainable and the rest are frozen.

questions.q: When might full fine-tuning still be the preferred choice over PEFT despite its higher cost?
options: Never -- PEFT is strictly better in every situation
When a team has ample multi-GPU compute, a large high-quality dataset, and needs the best achievable quality, especially for a large shift away from the base model's original distribution
Only when fine-tuning a model with fewer than 1 million parameters
Only when no GPU is available at all
questions.explain: Full fine-tuning retains a modest quality edge, particularly for large behavioral/domain shifts, and remains the right choice for teams with sufficient compute who prioritize maximum achievable quality.
